Work must be less than two years old (nothing made before 2025), must not have been exhibited at the League before, and framed or unframed may not exceed 48 inches on its longest side; sculpture should be small to medium in scale and weight. Hanging work must arrive wall-ready with wire — no sawtooth hangers — and the Exhibitions Director decides placement. Drop-off runs 12–18 July 2027 and unsold work is collected 23–26 August, after which unclaimed pieces incur $5 a day in storage.
Everything in the show must be for sale: nothing may be listed NFS, the artist sets the retail price, and the League keeps a 35% commission, paying the artist 65% monthly on sales. Twelve named awards are listed. The two largest are open to any medium — the Sarah Ethel Tunnell Award for Best in Show ($500) and the Mary Hall Leach Award for Outstanding Work ($250) — and photography has one award of its own, the William Horn Award for Best Photograph ($50). The rest are mostly medium-specific: the Delaware Watercolor Society Award of Excellence ($300), the Faucett Okie Emerging Delaware Artist Award ($300, oil or pastel in a traditional style, Delaware residents only, applied for by email with a statement), the Thomas McFarland Skelly Award for a painting of exceptional merit in any medium ($200), the Howard Schroeder Award for best portrait or figurative work ($100), the Mary Derrickson McCurdy Memorial Award for honourable mention ($100), the Connie Boland Award for best still life ($100), the Louise Chambers Corkran Award for best sculpture ($50), the Adelia E. Chiswell Award for outstanding watercolour ($50) and the Col. W.S. Corkran Award ($50) for the best painting of the Eastern Shore, also applied for by email. Selected works appear on the League's website and in its promotional, educational and press materials. — Deadline: July 16, 2027. Fee: $25 (RAL membership required, $50/year). Prize: $1,700 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Siena International Photo Awards 2027
item.description:
The Siena Awards' flagship contest, open to professional and amateur photographers worldwide, returns for 2027 with entries open since 11 October 2026 and a deadline of 7 January 2027. Ten categories are published: Journeys & Adventures; Fascinating Faces and Characters; The Beauty of Nature; Animals in Their Environment; Sports in Action; Story-Telling; Documentary & Photojournalism; Street Photography; Underwater Life; and Short Documentary Film. There is no limit on how many entries a photographer may make, published and previously awarded work is accepted, and there is no restriction on when a photograph was taken.
The first image is free to enter. Beyond that the published ladder is €30 for a bundle of three images including the free one, €10 for each additional image, and €35 each for a Story-Telling entry or a video; entries can be spread freely across categories and fees are non-refundable. As of 26 October 2026 the rules page still prints last cycle's early-bird window ("by December 1st, 2025" for a €20 three-image bundle, with uploads allowed until 2 December 2026), so treat any early-bird discount as unconfirmed for this edition and check before paying.
Prizes are weighted towards recognition rather than cash. The Photographer of the Year receives €1,500 worth of photographic equipment, the Pangea Prize crystal trophy and a fixed €400 towards two nights' accommodation in Siena for the ceremony weekend; Best Author, category winners and second and third places in each category receive the trophy and the same €400 accommodation contribution. Highly Commended entries receive a Crystal of Honor and Commended entries a parchment. The trophies and parchments are handed over only to winners who attend the ceremony in Siena, held each October at the Teatro dei Rinnovati, and winning images go into the "Imagine all the People Sharing all the World" group exhibition that runs for over a month during the Siena Awards Festival.
Photographers keep copyright; the organisers take a free licence to use entered images for promotion of the award and festival — catalogues, posters, websites and official merchandise — always with credit, and no entry is sold or used commercially by sponsors without the photographer's approval. Post-processing is limited to what could be achieved in a darkroom: cropping and brightness, contrast and colour adjustments are allowed, but key compositional elements may not be added or removed, and finalists must supply RAW files. AI-generated photographs are not accepted — the rules require images captured and edited by humans without AI algorithms. Entries are JPG, sRGB or Adobe98, 8-bit, no more than 1920 px on the longest side, with no watermarks or borders; finalists must be able to supply files of at least 2400 x 3600 px at 300 dpi. The jury page for this edition redirects to previous editions, so the 2027 panel is not yet published. — Deadline: January 7, 2027. Fee: Free (1 image); €30/3, €10 each extra. Prize: €1,500 gear + Pangea trophy + exhibition.

item.title: Solace in Silence · LightBox Photographic Gallery
item.description:
LightBox's winter members exhibit asks where you find solace and when you welcome silence: a winter's night with the moon reflecting on snow, a moment awake in a quiet house while others sleep, a stroll down a gravel lane at dusk. The gallery wants visuals of a momentary pause — the places and things that make you feel grounded, and where your mind reaches when you are stressed, grieving or weary, whether inside your home, in the vastness of wilderness, or in the delicacy of a flower. Against what the call describes as a day of rapid-fire imagery and political chaos, the show is pitched as a collective stilling of the mind.
The call is inclusive rather than competitive: LightBox states that every member who submits will be juried into the exhibit, with LightBox member Joni Kabana named as juror. Entry costs nothing, and members submit three to five images as jpgs of 1000 pixels in the long dimension, emailed with a completed entry form. The show runs 12 December 2026 – 30 January 2027 at the gallery on Marine Drive in Astoria, Oregon, and is carried on the gallery's social channels, show page and newsletter.
The gate is membership, not the entry fee, and the gallery's two tiers are not interchangeable for this show. LightBox's membership guidelines publish Supporting membership at $100 per calendar year — a 10% discount on prints, services and workshops, gallery support, library access and a member webpage — and Associate membership at $25 per month, which adds the Wednesday image-sharing evenings, first invites to special events, a flat $25-for-10 rate on LightBox juried group shows and, the line that matters here, participation in members group exhibits. The call page and the prospectus both say only “members of LightBox Photographic Gallery” without naming a tier, and the guidelines add that the gallery likes to treat all members the same whatever the level, so a Supporting member may well be welcome; but the only published benefit list puts this exhibit on the $25-a-month tier, so budget for that and ask the gallery before joining at the cheaper rate. Photographers interested in joining are asked to contact the gallery through its site.
Participants selected for the gallery have their work printed by LightBox at 50% of normal cost, at 9 x 13 up to 12 x 18 inches, matted and framed for the exhibit; bare prints can be collected at the gallery afterwards or shipped for $20. Members may instead send an original matted or framed print, with complimentary frame rental offered for the run of the show; work not printed by LightBox must reach the gallery by 9 December 2026. Gallery-printed bare prints carry a preset $200 price unless the artist asks that a work not be for sale, originals are priced as the member wishes, and the gallery keeps a 40% commission, paying artists within seven days of the show's close. Notification of accepted entries is 11 November 2026. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: Free (LightBox Associate membership required, $25/month). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Something Personal 2026 · APA San Francisco
item.description:
The 29th edition of Something Personal, the annual competition run by the San Francisco chapter of American Photographic Artists, is built entirely around work made for no client: images commissioned by a paying client for publication or another designated use do not qualify as personal work and may be disqualified. Entry is open to all photographers and all types of photography, with no theme and no categories beyond that distinction, and judging is blind — file names are hidden from the jurors and photographers' names are disclosed only after the process is complete.
The chapter selects a Top 100, shows the prints at an exhibition and industry event pitched at peers, art lovers and art buyers, and may include selected work in a photo book. APA SF describes an acclaimed judging panel and a lineup of prizes but publishes neither list, and the call sends entrants to the chapter site to see the growing list; as of 23 October 2026 that site carries nothing for this edition — the newest item on its exhibitions-and-contests index is the 2025 call for entries, and its past-judges and prize pages are dated 2016 and 2021 — so anyone deciding on the strength of the jury is paying before it is published.
Each entry fee covers one image, and a photographer may submit as many images as they like in batches of ten or fewer before the deadline. Non-members pay $35 an image; the member rates are $10 (student), $15 (ProPlus or Professional), $25 (Emerging or Supporter) and $30 (Contributor or Educator), and APA membership starts at $50 a year. Files are .jpg, sRGB, 72 ppi, at most 2 MB, at least 1,800 px on the short side and no more than 2,400 px on the long side, with the photographer's full name and the image title in the filename.
One cost sits past the entry fee: photographers selected for the Top 100 who want to be in the exhibition pay for their own printing and framing and must deliver prints to the chapter's designated framers by a deadline the chapter says is still to be announced. Entrants keep full copyright and grant APA SF only the rights named in the rules — exhibition and display at APA events, use on APA websites and in promotional material, and reproduction in APA-approved publications including photo books that may be sold to support the chapter. Entries close 20 November 2026, Top 100 notifications go out 1–5 December, and the print exhibition and industry event follow in January (the call's timeline prints "January 2026", which the rest of its own dates place in January 2027). — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $35 per image ($10–$30 APA members). Prize: Top 100 print exhibition + prizes.

item.title: Squared: a 12"x12" Exhibition · Deines Cultural Center
item.description:
A judged small-format show at the Deines Cultural Center in Russell, Kansas — a three-gallery centre whose permanent collection includes wood engravings by Prairie Printmaker E. Hubert Deines — that asks artists to work inside one fixed dimension: every piece must measure 12 by 12 inches, excluding framing. The centre frames it as a community-centred exhibition that makes space for both emerging and established voices and puts work in front of new audiences and a network of regional artists.
All mediums are encouraged with three exclusions — no installation art, no video and no artificial-intelligence work — and the centre also asks artists not to submit copies, kits or giclée reproductions. Photography is not named in the call, but nothing in it excludes photographs, and the centre's previous juried call named photography explicitly among the accepted media.
An artist may enter up to three original works in one submission for a $12 fee. Work must have been made in the last three years, must not have been exhibited at the Deines Cultural Center before, and must arrive ready to hang and for sale; no substitution or modification of an accepted work is allowed. Acceptances go out on 17 January 2027, accepted work must reach the centre by 3 February, judging happens in person, and awards are announced at the reception on 7 February 2027 — the award amounts are not published in the call. Entrants who cannot attend are notified by email on 9 February. The centre keeps a 25% commission on sales, and shipping is entirely at the artist’s cost: shipped work must arrive with a prepaid return label, cash is not accepted for return postage, and the gallery disclaims liability for damage before, during or after the exhibition.
The call says it is "open to regional artists, both amateur and professional" without saying how far the region reaches, and the centre's own website carries no page for this exhibition; artists outside Kansas should check with the centre before paying the fee, through the contact form at deinesculturalcenter.org/contact.html or on 785-483-3742. — Deadline: January 9, 2027. Fee: $12. Prize: Group exhibition + awards.

item.title: 41st Annual West Michigan Art Competition · Lowell Arts
item.description:
Lowell Arts' 41st annual juried competition for artists living in a 42-county region of lower West Michigan, shown in the gallery in historic downtown Lowell from 6 February to 27 March 2027. Work in all visual art media is considered, and the prospectus names photography and digital art explicitly, asking that traditional print media, photography and digital art be from a limited edition; commercial reproductions, including giclée prints, are not accepted. Video entries may not be submitted.
$4,000 in cash awards is presented: five awards of $500, ten honorable mentions of $100, a $250 ceramics award sponsored by the West Michigan Potters Guild and a $250 fiber arts award sponsored by the Woodland Weavers & Spinners. The juror is not named on either Lowell Arts' own page or the CaFÉ prospectus.
An artist may enter one piece only, documented with at least two and no more than five images of that piece; the first image must show the work in its entirety, and incomplete entries are not juried. Work must be original, completed in the last three years and not previously exhibited at Lowell Arts. Two-dimensional entries may be no larger than 62 inches in any direction including the frame, must be framed or fitted for hanging with secure wire (no sawtooth hangers, no exposed glass edges), and three-dimensional work must fit through a standard door frame. Entry is $40, reduced to $30 for Lowell Arts members and for students over 18 with a college ID — the discount code must be requested from the gallery by phone before entering, and a membership must run through March 2027 to qualify.
Accepted work is hand-delivered to Lowell Arts (223 W Main St) on 28–30 January 2027, or shipped prepaid to arrive by Friday 29 January with a prepaid return label enclosed; all packing and shipping costs fall to the artist. Work must stay up for the run of the show and is collected 30 March to 2 April. Lowell Arts takes 30% commission on sales and recommends, but does not require, that work be for sale. Entrants must live in one of the 42 eligible counties: Allegan, Antrim, Barry, Benzie, Berrien, Branch, Calhoun, Cass, Charlevoix, Cheboygan, Clare, Clinton, Crawford, Eaton, Emmet, Grand Traverse, Gratiot, Hillsdale, Ingham, Ionia, Isabella, Jackson, Kalamazoo, Kalkaska, Kent, Lake, Leelanau, Manistee, Mason, Mecosta, Missaukee, Montcalm, Muskegon, Newaygo, Oceana, Osceola, Otsego, Ottawa, Roscommon, St. Joseph, Van Buren and Wexford. — Deadline: January 5, 2027. Fee: $40 ($30 members / students). Prize: $4,000 in cash awards.

item.title: By Hand: An Exhibition of Contemporary Alternative Process Photography · Texas Photographic Society
item.description:
Texas Photographic Society's sixth By Hand exhibition is a call for hand-made photo-based imagery made with alternative photographic processes and historical printing methods. The juror is Jill Enfield, a fine art photographer, author and educator who teaches hand colouring, wet plate collodion and other processes at Parsons, New York University, Long Island University, the International Center of Photography and RISD, and who wrote Photo Imaging: A Complete Guide to Alternative Processes and Jill Enfield's Guide to Photographic Alternative Processes.
The process list is long and explicitly open-ended: Albumen, Anthotype, Argyrotype, Athenatype, Bayard Direct Positive, Calotype, Carbon, Casein, Chrysotype, Cyanotype, Dusting-On, Gum Bichromate, Gumoil, Herschel's Breath Printing, Inkjet Photopolymer Gravure, Ivorytype, Kallitype, Mordançage, Platinum/Palladium, POP, Solarplate Intaglio, Van Dyke Brown, Wet Plate Collodion, Whey Process, Ziatype, and any photographic image-making technique that incorporates printmaking, ceramics or painting. TPS notes that non-framed and three-dimensional work is now allowed, a change from earlier editions, and refers entrants to an “if your work is accepted” section for the presentation rules that go with it — that section appears nowhere on the CaFÉ record, and TPS has no page for this edition yet, so the framing and delivery requirements cannot be read anywhere today.
Entry is $30 for current TPS members and $40 for non-members, each covering five images, plus $5 for every additional image up to twelve; one submission per artist. Membership is not required to enter, and an entrant who joins or renews at the same time pays the $30 member rate (memberships start at $20 for students and military). All entry and membership fees are non-refundable. Awards are $400 for first place, $250 for second and $150 for third, with up to five Honorable Mentions.
The call is open to artists internationally at any level who are 18 or older at the time of entry. Work shown previously in a TPS exhibition is not eligible, and TPS board members may enter but cannot win awards. Entries are 5 to 12 images; no audio or video.
The call opened October 22 2026 and closes December 20 2026 at 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time. TPS's prospectus names the venue twice as the Wilma and Terence Dennis Gallery at Austin College in Sherman, Texas, opening February 8 2027 and running to March 26 2027, while its own calendar block still carries the previous edition's venue line — "Exhibition opens at the Center for Contemporary Arts" — and asks for work to be delivered to Abilene, Texas, on February 2 2027. Confirm the delivery address with TPS before shipping. The calendar also dates the notification "January 15, 2026", which falls before the deadline, so no results date is stored here. — Deadline: December 20, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $40 non-members / 5 images + $5 each. Prize: $400 / $250 / $150.

item.title: As Much Truth As One Can Bear · Arts Center in Orange
item.description:
The Arts Center in Orange, on East Main Street in Orange, Virginia, is running a juried exhibition built on James Baldwin's essay and proposition about truth. The show runs from 5 February to 27 March 2027.
Eligibility is the first thing to check. The call is open to emerging and established artists of African American heritage, students included, who are 18 or older. All media are accepted, and the centre's list names photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, digital and text-based work, video and textiles.
There are three cash prizes, $1,500 for first place, $1,000 for second and $500 for third. The page heads them "Up to $3000 in awards and more" without saying what the more is. No juror is named. The page does list the selection criteria: conceptual strength, originality, relevance to the theme, technical quality and emotional impact.
The brief asks artists not to illustrate Baldwin or his biography. It asks for work about identity, race, memory, justice, love and survival, and about personal or collective truths, visibility, silence or resistance.
Entries go by email, with "As Much Truth As One Can Bear" in the subject line. Applicants send 5–10 images or time-based samples of recent work, an artist statement of 300–500 words and a CV or short biography, and pay the $20 fee through the centre's online shop. The exhibition is physical. Artists who can't deliver and collect in person pay for shipping to the centre, and return shipping help is possible if the work arrives in a reusable UPS box with a prepaid return label. — Deadline: December 30, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: $1,500 + $1,000 + $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: How to Hold Time · Arts Center in Orange
item.description:
How to Hold Time is a juried group exhibition at the Arts Center in Orange, Virginia, for artists aged 65 and over. It runs from 4 June to 31 July 2027. One line on the page calls it Hold On to Time, but the heading, the web address and the email subject line all use How to Hold Time.
Applicants must be 65 or older and show an ongoing, active creative practice. The call is open to local, national and international artists. All media are welcome, and photography is named in the list with painting, sculpture, installation, video and textiles.
The prizes total $2,500. Best in Show receives $1,000, first prize $650, second $350 and third $200, and three Juror's Choice winners receive $100 each. No juror is named yet.
The theme comes from one of Pablo Neruda's Elemental Odes, which describes time as two rivers, one running back over life already lived and one moving forward with the present, joined for a single instant. The centre asks for work that holds time rather than represents it, memory against immediacy, erosion against revelation, and says entries don't need to illustrate the poem.
Entries go by email with "How to Hold Time" in the subject line. Applicants send 5–10 images or time-based samples of recent work, a 300–500 word artist statement, a CV or short biography highlighting continued practice, and an optional reflection on time in their work. The $20 fee is paid through the centre's online shop. Artists who can't deliver and collect in person pay for shipping to the centre, and return shipping help is possible with a reusable UPS box and a prepaid return label. — Deadline: February 26, 2027. Fee: $20. Prize: $1,000 + $650 + $350 + $200 + 3×$100 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Mini Masters Show · Arts Center in Orange
item.description:
The Mini Masters Show is a juried group exhibition of small works at the Arts Center in Orange, Virginia, from 4 December 2026 to 30 January 2027. Every work in it measures 8 by 8 inches.
Entry is free. Artists propose three original works, each 8 × 8 inches not counting the frame. The page's opening describes the show as one of 8-inch paintings, but its media section says any medium that can be framed and exhibited on a wall is welcome, which takes in photographic prints. Work must arrive framed and ready to hang, with mats and frames kept minimal because they add to the size. Only canvas may hang unframed, and only with clean, wrapped edges.
There are no prizes. Every accepted work is offered for sale at a fixed $100, and sales are split evenly between the artist and the centre, so the artist receives $50 for each work sold.
Delivery is the artist's job. Work is dropped off on Saturday 28 November 2026 and unsold work is collected on Saturday 30 January 2027. Unlike the centre's other calls, this page offers no shipping arrangement.
Applicants email 5–10 images or time-based samples of recent work, an artist statement of 300–500 words, a CV and a short biography, with "Mini Masters" in the subject line. The three 8-inch pieces don't need to be finished at the time of applying. An optional reflection on scale, intimacy or time in the work can be added. The centre says it is looking for originality, craftsmanship and a compelling visual voice, in minimal or layered, narrative or abstract work. — Deadline: November 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence 2027 · agalab
item.description:
agalab (Amsterdams Grafisch Atelier) is a printmaking workshop in Amsterdam that runs a year-round artist-in-residence programme. It offers six places, two with a guest room beside the workshop and four without accommodation. Residencies run in monthly cycles, from the first Monday to the last Friday of the month, for one to three months, and the 2027 application form lists a cycle for every month of the year.
The residency is self-funded. agalab's own page prices it at €500 a month without accommodation, €1,450 a month with a room (own shower, shared toilets and kitchen, washing machine and dryer, and a bicycle), and €750 for a duo. Materials are not included. Residents pay a €100 downpayment and log their costs on a sheet, and the unused balance is returned at the end. Artists who graduated between 2024 and 2026 can apply for a 50% subsidised place, accommodation not included. Technical introductions beyond the standard ones cost €55 an hour.
Residents have 24/7 access to the workshop. Technicians are on hand Monday to Thursday, silkscreen on Monday and Tuesday, intaglio, relief and lithography on Wednesday and Thursday. Techniques include silkscreen on paper and textile, drypoint and aquatint etching, Toyobo photopolymer plates, stone lithography, linocut, woodcut and letterpress. For photographers, the darkroom has a Durst enlarger, developing tanks for 35mm and 120 film, and a basic stock of developer, stop bath and fixer.
The month has a set shape. Week one brings introductions to the silkscreen and etching workshops, week three a mid-residency studio conversation with the team, a visiting artist and the other residents, and week four an exhibition at agalab's Open Day.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, with a reply within about four weeks. The programme is aimed at artists with some printmaking experience, but the page says artists with little or none are also welcome to apply. Applicants email the form with a project plan of up to 120 words, a motivation letter, a CV and a portfolio of up to 20 MB. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: €500–€1,450/month (self-funded). Prize: Residency + Exhibition.

item.title: The Family — Lineage, Choice, and the Album · Der Greif
item.description: A new edition of Der Greif Pulse, the Munich non-profit's online exhibition strand, opened on 22 October 2026 and looking beyond the traditional family portrait. The call addresses family in every form — "whether through bloodline, heritage, or chosen community" — and encourages work on the performance of familial roles and on the deliberate choices behind what gets preserved in the album versus what stays unrecorded. Der Greif names vernacular archive interventions, intimate documentary projects, staged visual narratives and conceptual studies of shared memory among the approaches it wants, and asks what "the family photo" means today. Submit one project of at least 10 images; the conditions of participation state that video is not part of the submission format for this round, and projects previously selected in a Der Greif opportunity should not be re-submitted. Selected artists get an online exhibition in the Pulse section and a place in an online roundtable critique session with peers facilitated by Der Greif staff, plus visibility across the organisation's international community; they may also be invited to submit a portfolio to Der Greif Studio, which opens routes to artwork sales and commissions. Selection is judged on artistic quality, conceptual clarity, openness to dialogue and process, and engagement with identity and community. Entry is free — Der Greif, a registered non-profit, suggests a voluntary €10 donation and will issue a 50% or 100% discount voucher on request to anyone unable to contribute. The call is international with no age or regional restrictions and is aimed particularly at emerging and mid-career artists. Results are announced in November 2026 and the online exhibition follows in December 2026. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: Free (voluntary €10 donation). Prize: Online exhibition + Group critique session.
